ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, $DC\parallel AB$, $BA=BC$, $AE\perp BC$ with the foot of the perpendicular being point E, and point F is the midpoint of $AC$. Is $\angle AFB=90^\circ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Proof: \\
Since $BA = BC$, and $F$ is the midpoint of $AC$, \\
therefore $BF \perp AC$. \\
Therefore, $\angle AFB = 90^\circ$. \\
Hence, the answer is $\boxed{90^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, D is at the upper left, and C is above and located between A and B; AB is the base, DC is above and parallel to AB, and AD vertically connects A and D. Line segment AC has been drawn, and point F is marked on AC; line segment BF connects from B to F. Point E is on BC, and AE is also drawn. The problem asks whether the angle ∠AFB formed by FA and FB at point F is 90°. Then reason: From the given BA=BC, it can be known that triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle with B as the vertex and AC as the base. Also because F is the midpoint of AC, BF is the median drawn from the vertex B of the isosceles triangle to the base AC. In an isosceles triangle, the median from the vertex angle's vertex to the midpoint of the base is also perpendicular to the base, so BF ⟂ AC. Since AF is a part of AC, BF ⟂ AF, that is, ∠AFB=90°.
